name: Huntington Ingalls Industries, Inc.
reason: Sole US builder of nuclear carriers and one of two nuclear-sub yards gives a multi-decade, backlog-visible franchise; EBIT margin 4.9% sits near a trough vs 12.9% peak (27th pctile) with EPS 0.81x 10y max, net debt/EBITDA 2.4x and consensus FY1-FY3 EPS growth 13-21% as margins recover.

name: Archrock, Inc.
reason: Gas compression tied to upstream activity, with EBIT margin at a 10y high (38.7%, 100th pctile), EPS 1.0x 10y max, shares +9.8%/yr and acquisitions 1.17x FCF; ROIC averages just 2.2%.

name: Synchrony Financial
reason: Private-label card lender whose earnings are set by the consumer credit cycle and late-fee regulation; EPS at 1.0x 10y peak after 2020 fell 48%, cheap (7.3x) but not special.

name: MPLX LP
reason: Midstream MLP dependent on commodity volumes and its refiner parent, with units growing 26%/yr, net debt/EBITDA 3.9x, margin near 10y high and negative consensus LTG.

name: Marriott Vacations Worldwide Corp.
reason: Timeshare developer/lender exposed to consumer credit and discretionary travel with net debt/EBITDA 7.1x, ROIC ~2.9% and adjusted EPS 87% above GAAP.

name: NGL Energy Partners LP
reason: Energy logistics MLP with GAAP losses in 8 of the last 10 years, net debt/EBITDA 5.2x, acquisitions 6x FCF and earnings tied to Permian activity and commodity spreads.

name: Mechanics Bancorp
reason: Newly combined bank (HomeStreet reverse merger) with losses in 2023-24, shares +26%/yr and EPS only 0.15x 10y max, so the go-forward franchise cannot yet be forecast.

name: The Mosaic Co.
reason: Phosphate/potash earnings set by fertilizer and crop prices (EPS swung 0.19 to 11.01 over 10y), ROIC ~5%, consensus FY1 EPS -83%.

name: Nutex Health, Inc.
reason: Micro-hospital operator whose recent profits (after a decade of losses, shares +164%/yr) rely heavily on out-of-network arbitration awards under the No Surprises Act, a credible regulatory/reimbursement threat.

name: Marathon Petroleum Corp.
reason: Refiner whose EPS is driven by crack spreads (2.45 in 2021 to 26.16 in 2022 to 10.70 in 2025) with net debt/EBITDA 3.1x; consensus FY1-FY3 path (+511% then -51%) shows it is unforecastable.

name: WillScot Holdings Corp.
reason: Modular/storage rental roll-up with acquisitions 1.66x FCF, net debt/EBITDA 4.2x, adjusted EPS far above GAAP and EPS down 26% in 2025 as non-residential construction slowed.

name: Expedia Group, Inc.
reason: EPS at 1.0x 10y max with EBIT margin at a 10y high (13.4%, 100th pctile) and adjusted EPS ~2x GAAP, while AI agents and Google threaten OTA traffic acquisition within 5 years.

name: TripAdvisor, Inc.
reason: Declining metasearch/review traffic with EPS CAGR -4.7% over 10y and only 2/9 years of 7%+ growth, plus acute AI-search disintermediation risk.

name: Black Stone Minerals LP
reason: Mineral royalty earnings are set by oil and gas prices and operator drilling (EPS 2.12 in 2022 vs 1.28 in 2025, FY1 -20%), no route to controllable growth.

name: Yelp, Inc.
reason: Local-ads platform with margin at a 10y high (12.6%, 100th pctile), FY1 EPS -19.5%, decelerating revenue and direct exposure to AI-search disintermediation; cheap at 8.2x but not special.

name: Post Holdings, Inc.
reason: Cereal/egg/food roll-up in a shrinking RTE cereal category with acquisitions 1.48x FCF, net debt/EBITDA 5.5x and ROIC ~2.5%; growth bought, not earned.

name: Diamondback Energy, Inc.
reason: Permian E&P whose earnings track oil prices (EPS 24.04 in 2022 to 13.37 in 2025) and acquisitions 1.36x FCF with shares +16.5%/yr.

name: Supernus Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
reason: CNS specialty pharma facing generic erosion of legacy franchises, with EBIT margin now -5.2% (9th pctile) and growth reliant on acquisitions (0.93x FCF, Sage); patent-cliff threat fails the test.

name: Delek Logistics Partners LP
reason: Logistics MLP dependent on its refiner sponsor with net debt/EBITDA 7.6x, acquisitions 1.35x FCF and units growing 8.2%/yr; EPS CAGR only 2.7%.

name: Citizens Financial Group, Inc. (Rhode Island)
reason: Spread-dependent regional bank with ROE averaging 7.4%, EPS 0.75x 2021 peak and no evident deposit or underwriting edge; ordinary, rate-cycle driven.
